  • Method Details

    • create

      <T extends Config> T create(Class<? extends T> clazz, Map<?,?>... imports)
      Creates a Config instance from the specified interface

      Imports are merged into a Properties instance, whose contract only admits String keys and values. Entries with a null or non-String key or value are therefore rejected, rather than being accepted and then silently ignored when the properties are read.

      Type Parameters:
      T - type of the interface.
      Parameters:
      clazz - the interface extending from Config that you want to instantiate.
      imports - additional variables to be used to resolve the properties.
      Returns:
      an object implementing the given interface, which maps methods to property values.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if any of the imports contains a null or non-String key or value.
      Since:
      1.0.5

    • setProperty

      String setProperty(String key, String value)
      Set a property in the ConfigFactory. Those properties will be used to expand variables specified in the `@Source` annotation, or by the ConfigFactory to configure its own behavior.

      The properties understood by the factory itself are, all of them since 2.0.0:

      • owner.key.prefix: a literal prepended to the key of every property, for the interfaces that do not declare a Config.Prefix of their own.
      • owner.key.prefix.from.package: true derives that prefix from the package of the interface declaring the method, followed by a dot.
      • owner.strict: true turns this library's warnings into refusals, so that a configuration which would have carried on with its default values does not get created at all. The default is false, which is how OWNER has always behaved. What it covers is not a list of its own — it is the warnings, and those already leave the legitimate cases alone: a source that is merely absent stays silent under it too, since Config.LoadType.FIRST expects misses by design.
      • owner.declared.only: true restricts every Accessible view and Object.toString() to the properties each interface declares, for the interfaces that do not carry Config.DeclaredOnly — the ones you did not write. An interface that carries the annotation decides for itself, in both directions.

      They are read when a Config object is created, and the object keeps them for the rest of its life.

      Parameters:
      key - the key for the property.
      value - the value for the property.
      Returns:
      the old value.
      Since:
      1.0.5

    • registerLoader

      void registerLoader(Loader loader)
      Registers a loader to enables additional file formats.

      A registered loader comes first, both when a source is being matched to a loader and among the file names looked for when a configuration declares no Config.Sources. It therefore takes precedence over the built-in loaders and can take over a source one of them would have accepted.

      Registering is one of the two ways in, and it is the explicit one: a loader declared in META-INF/services/org.aeonbits.owner.loaders.Loader is found on the classpath without this call. See Loader for the difference, which matters in a container.

      Parameters:
      loader - the loader to register.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the specified loader is null.
      Since:
      1.0.5

    • registerValueHandler

      void registerValueHandler(ValueHandler handler)
      Registers a handler a value can name, as ${$name::payload}, instead of holding its own text.

      A handler is registered under its own name, and registering one under a name already taken replaces it - which is what makes a key rotation an ordinary thing to do.

      Registration is the only way in: unlike a Loader, a handler is not discovered on the classpath. It is also what settles where a handler's own configuration comes from, since the caller constructs the instance and hands it over already holding its passphrase, token or endpoint.

      A configuration keeps the handlers the factory held when it was created, so register before create(Class, Map[]).

      Parameters:
      handler - the handler to register.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the handler is null, or its name is null, empty or contains whitespace or any of $ : { }.
      Since:
      2.0.0
